data.text:
I have enough evidence from the watchdog records and direct probes. Key findings:

- **WAN link physically up**: `ifconfig vtnet0` shows UP/RUNNING/LOWER_UP with lease `198.51.100.27`; `arp -n` resolves the gateway `198.51.100.1` (modem MAC present).
- **Upstream dead**: `ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1` → 100% loss to the ISP gateway/modem.
- **Watchdog timeline** (`events.jsonl` / `modem-events.jsonl`): outage began ~02:01:44 with modem `No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out`, then `TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND` at 02:14:10, then modem rebooted and `registration complete` at 02:28:21. Metrics go `NOT_SYNCHRONIZED` (02:06) → `OPERATIONAL` (02:29, 02:40).
- The watchdog is in **observe mode**: it logged `would_reload` at 02:30 and 02:40 but never actually reconfigured the WAN, so the firewall's WAN side was never refreshed after the modem recovered/re-registered.

data.reason: The ISP link dropped around 02:01 when the cable modem lost upstream sync (T3 timeout / No Ranging Response, plus a TFTP config-file-not-found during re-registration); the modem only completed re-registration ~02:28, and because the WAN watchdog runs in observe mode the firewall's WAN interface was never reloaded/renewed afterward, so internet traffic still cannot reach the ISP gateway.

data.cause: The ISP link dropped around 02:01 when the cable modem lost upstream sync (T3 timeout / No Ranging Response, plus a TFTP config-file-not-found during re-registration); the modem only completed re-registration ~02:28, and because the WAN watchdog runs in observe mode the firewall's WAN interface was never reloaded/renewed afterward, so internet traffic still cannot reach the ISP gateway.
evidence: ifconfig vtnet0: state UP,RUNNING,LOWER_UP with inet 198.51.100.27 — local WAN interface itself is up
arp -n: gateway 198.51.100.1 resolves to 00:17:10:9a:a3:96 (modem) — L2 path to modem exists
ping -c 3 -n 198.51.100.1: 3 packets transmitted, 0 received, 100% packet loss — cannot reach ISP gateway

/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-events.jsonl: 02:01:44 'No Ranging Response received - T3 time-out'; 02:14:10 'TFTP failed - configuration file NOT FOUND'; 02:28:21 'Cable Modem Reboot ... registration complete'
/var/db/wan-watchdog/modem-metrics.jsonl: status NOT_SYNCHRONIZED at 02:06 then OPERATIONAL at 02:29 and 02:40
/var/db/wan-watchdog/events.jsonl: mode=observe; decisions 'would_reload' at 02:30 and 02:40 — no actual WAN reload was performed after the modem recovered
data.recommendation: Reload/reconfigure the WAN interface on gw.lan to renew its DHCP lease and re-establish the upstream session now that the modem has re-registered (registration complete ~02:28). This is exactly what the observe-mode watchdog wanted to do. Longer term, switch the watchdog out of observe mode so it can auto-reload WAN once the modem returns to OPERATIONAL, and have the ISP investigate the upstream T3/Ranging loss and the missing DOCSIS config file (TFTP NOT FOUND) that triggered the outage.
data.detail: WAN not re-established after modem lost sync and re-registered
